name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Tankers hit mines near Hormuz 19–20 Nov
summary: Iran says tankers hit its mines near Hormuz on 19–20 Nov; at least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November
state: Iran's military said tankers that had switched off tracking caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz on 19–20 Nov, claims not independently confirmed (Anadolu; Tasnim). Washington Institute data cited by AAP count at least 10 ships hit in the first 10 days of November after 37 attacks in October (Canberra Times). Mines and repeated attacks keep Hormuz traffic materially impeded.
for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice for the Gulf. Shipping disruption can delay deliveries and raise prices for fuel and imported goods.

sources.title: Anadolu — 2 oil tankers catch fire after hitting mines in waters east of Strait of Hormuz
Tasnim — Tanker catches fire after hitting sea mine in Strait of Hormuz
Canberra Times — Iran's military reports explosions on two oil tankers

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
